title: Spotify’s new tool aims to stop deepfakes from being attributed to real artists
slides: Can Spotify stop AI from faking real artists?
A new tool targets deepfakes attributed to them
But it flags impersonation, not all synthetic music
Artists must opt in to be protected
Check if your favorite artist is covered
thread_text:
1. Spotify's new weapon

A tool now flags deepfakes attributed to real artists on the platform, but it only targets impersonation, not all synthetic music.

2. The opt-in catch

Artists must actively opt in to be protected, leaving many unaware or unrepresented.

3. Limited scope

The tool doesn't catch AI-generated tracks that mimic style without direct attribution, so plenty of synthetic music slips through.

4. Fan's responsibility

Listeners can check if their favorite artist is covered, but the burden shouldn't fall on them.

5. Take action today

Search Spotify's artist protection list and see if your favorite is enrolled. If not, ask why.

instagram.caption:
Spotify’s new tool flags deepfakes attributed to real artists, but only if those artists have opted in.

It targets impersonation, not all synthetic music, so AI tracks that mimic a style without naming a real artist still slip through 🔊

That means your favorite artist might not be protected yet, and the burden falls on listeners to check the list.

If you create or publish music, this opt-in gap could affect how your voice or brand gets used 👀

Search Spotify’s artist protection list today and see if your favorite is enrolled. If not, ask why 🤔
